classification.difficultyReason: Combines several angle relationships in composite and overlapping figures.

children.label: a
children.prompt: $PQRS$ is a square and $PQT$ is an equilateral triangle.

spec.description: Upright square, inverted equilateral triangle sharing its top side, and a segment from the triangle's lower vertex to the square's lower-right corner. The lower-left right-angle marker is retained.
spec.mathematics: Square and equilateral-triangle geometry determines the angle sectors. Internal coordinate names are not printed source labels.
spec.answerVisibility: No numerical solution annotations appear in the question figure.

answer.short: Top corners: $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ each. Interior vertex: $60^\circ$, $75^\circ$ and reflex $225^\circ$. Bottom-right corner: $15^\circ$ and $75^\circ$. Each unsplit square corner is $90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Each angle of the equilateral triangle is $60^\circ$, and each square corner is $90^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}90^\circ-60^\circ&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
The triangle formed by the top-right corner, the interior vertex and the bottom-right corner is isosceles: its square side and equilateral-triangle side are equal. Its angle at the top-right corner is $30^\circ$, so its other two angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}2a+30^\circ&=180^\circ\\2a&=150^\circ\\a&=75^\circ\end{align*}$$
The remaining angle at the bottom-right corner and the reflex angle at the interior vertex are
$$\begin{align*}90^\circ-75^\circ&=15^\circ\\360^\circ-60^\circ-75^\circ&=225^\circ.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: This diagram shows two overlapping parallelograms.

spec.description: Two parallelograms share the lower horizontal side. Their inner sloping sides cross above that side.
spec.mathematics: The unsolved Word figure supplies 110 degrees at the upper-right corner of the left parallelogram and 130 degrees at the upper-left corner of the right parallelogram.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the independently identified original givens 110 and 130 degrees appear.

answer.short: Upper corners: $70^\circ$, $110^\circ$, $130^\circ$, $50^\circ$. Lower-left split: $60^\circ$, $50^\circ$. Lower-right split: $70^\circ$, $60^\circ$. Crossing: $60^\circ$, $120^\circ$, $60^\circ$, $120^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal; adjacent angles are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}180^\circ-110^\circ&=70^\circ\\180^\circ-130^\circ&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
The whole lower-left angle of the left parallelogram is $110^\circ$. The whole lower-right angle of the right parallelogram is $130^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}110^\circ-50^\circ&=60^\circ\\130^\circ-70^\circ&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
The triangle below the crossing has base angles $50^\circ$ and $70^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x+50^\circ+70^\circ&=180^\circ\\x&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
The vertically opposite crossing angle is also $60^\circ$. Each adjacent crossing angle is
$$\begin{align*}180^\circ-60^\circ&=120^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Apex-to-foot and left-vertex-to-foot segments meet at a right angle. The foot and right vertex lie on an extended horizontal baseline.
spec.mathematics: Original givens are 40 degrees at the left apex sector, 9 degrees between the leftward baseline and the foot-to-left-vertex ray, 134 degrees at the right exterior angle, and a right angle at the foot.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens appear. The 9-degree label is placed with its actual sector at the foot.

answer.short: Left vertex: $50^\circ$. Right apex sector: $53^\circ$. Foot-to-right-baseline sector: $81^\circ$. Right interior angle: $46^\circ$.
answer.worked:
In the left right-angled triangle,
$$\begin{align*}a+40^\circ+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\a&=50^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Angles above the straight baseline at the foot give
$$\begin{align*}b+90^\circ+9^\circ&=180^\circ\\b&=81^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The right interior angle and its exterior angle are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}c+134^\circ&=180^\circ\\c&=46^\circ.\end{align*}$$
In the right triangle,
$$\begin{align*}d+81^\circ+46^\circ&=180^\circ\\d&=53^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upper-left and lower-right triangles meet at the intersection of a horizontal line and a sloping straight line. Matching arrows identify the parallel outer sides.
spec.mathematics: Original givens are 53 degrees at the upper triangle's left baseline vertex and 67 degrees at the lower apex. The outer sides are parallel.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 53 and 67 degrees are supplied in the question.

answer.worked:
The upper apex angle is $67^\circ$ because alternate angles on parallel lines are equal. The right baseline angle is $53^\circ$ for the same reason, using the horizontal transversal.
In the upper triangle,
$$\begin{align*}x+53^\circ+67^\circ&=180^\circ\\x&=60^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The lower triangle's angle at the intersection is also $60^\circ$ because vertically opposite angles are equal.
